claim: Ayutthaya sits ~1.5 hours from Bangkok with typical guided day tours running 9-9.5 hours including transfers, lunch, and entry to 4 main temples
quote: A taxi journey takes approximately 1 hour and costs around $35. Guided day trips typically run 9-9.5 hours... Tours usually cost around 1,000-1,500 THB

claim: Viator's Ayutthaya day tour visits Wat Mahathat (Buddha-head-in-tree-roots), Wat Yai Chai Mongkhon, Wat Chaiwatthanaram and Wat Phra Si Sanphet
quote: Temples of Ayutthaya Day Tour from Bangkok

claim: Damnoen Saduak and Maeklong Railway are ~20km apart so they combine into a single 7-8 hour day trip from Bangkok; Maeklong train passes at 8:30, 11:10, 14:30, 17:40
quote: Train arrivals occur at exactly 8:30 AM, 11:10 AM, 2:30 PM, and 5:40 PM daily... A day trip to the markets from Bangkok takes around 7 to 8 hours

claim: Combined small-group Maeklong + Damnoen Saduak tours bookable on Viator with morning pickup from Bangkok hotels
quote: Maeklong Railway, Damnoen Saduak Floating Markets from Bangkok

claim: Bang Krachao is the green-lung peninsula in the Chao Phraya horseshoe (Phra Pradaeng), protected from high-rise/factory development, with bicycles renting for 50 THB/hour or 100 THB/day
quote: Bicycles are available for 50 THB per hour, or 100 THB for the whole day... No sky-rise buildings or commercial factories are allowed in Bang Krachao

claim: Half-day small-group cycling tours of Bang Krachao pass through villages, mangrove forest and farmland and are offered year-round
quote: Small-Group Half-Day Cycling Tour to Bangkok's Green Lung

claim: Wat Pho Thai Traditional Medical and Massage School opened in 1955 as the first Thai Medical School approved by the Thai Ministry of Education, codifying Thai massage as a formal discipline
quote: Wat Pho Thai Traditional Medical and Massage School was opened in 1955 inside Wat Pho. It is the first Thai Medical School under the approval of Thai Ministry of Education

claim: Wat Pho massage school charges roughly 340/520/1,040 THB for 30/60/120-minute Thai or foot massage with the temple admission at THB 300 since 2024
quote: Thai massage is available for 30/60/120 minutes at 340/520/1,040 Baht, and foot massage for the same durations costs 340/520/1,040 Baht

claim: Health Land Asoke offers a 2-hour traditional Thai massage at ~650-700 THB (about USD 18-20) and operates multiple Bangkok branches including Sathorn and Ekkamai
quote: excellent 2-hour Thai massage service for 650 baht... customers report paying 650 THB for a two-hour massage that was absolutely worth every baht

claim: Divana Virtue Spa charges ~2,150 THB for a 90-minute Siamese (Thai) massage and 2,350 THB for a 90-minute aromatherapy body massage, both including an Ashiyu foot soak
quote: Siamese Massage (traditional Thai massage) available for 2,150 THB for 90 minutes... Aromatherapy Body Massage at Divana Virtue Spa costs 2,350 THB for 90 minutes

claim: Manohra's restored teak rice-barge dinner cruise on the Chao Phraya starts at THB 3,500 net per person (soft drinks) and THB 4,500 with free-flow wine/beer
quote: starting at THB 3,500 net per person with free flow soft drink, THB 4,500 net per person with free flow wine, beer and soft drink

claim: Wan Fah dinner cruise on a converted teak rice-barge offers a 2-hour Chao Phraya dinner from around THB 1,100 per person, a more budget-friendly alternative to Manohra
quote: Wan Fah Dinner Cruise - Ticket price 1,100 Baht

claim: Longtail-boat klong tours through Thonburi's canals typically run ~750 THB/person for 1 hour or 1,000 THB for 90 minutes in high season, often stopping at Wat Paknam and Baan Silapin
quote: During the high season, prices are fixed at 750 THB per person for a 1-hour trip or 1,000 THB per person for 90-minute tours

claim: Banyan Tree Spa Bangkok occupies 1,101 sqm across three floors with 16 treatment suites in the Sathorn tower, open 10am-8pm and signature Royal Banyan uses warm sesame-oil herbal pouches
quote: 1,101 square meters across three floors, including 16 spa treatment suites, and is open daily from 10 am to 8 pm... Royal Banyan... featuring a warm herbal pouch dipped in Sesame Oil
